meta.description: Approved plain-language definitions. General explanations only, not personalized advice. The agent selects these; it does not write its own tax or legal rules. source_id and also_heard_as are optional additions.

glossary.plain: A retirement account that holds money moved from an earlier workplace retirement plan.
also_heard_as: retirement money from my old job
the account from my last employer

glossary.plain: A type of retirement account generally funded with money that has already been taxed. Withdrawal rules vary.
Money taken out of a retirement account. Taxes and other rules may apply.
also_heard_as: taking money out of my retirement

glossary.plain: Taking money out of an account. For retirement accounts this is often called a distribution.
An account that holds investments such as stocks, bonds, and funds, without the special rules of a retirement account.
The person or organization you name to receive an account if you pass away.
Moving money or investments from one account to another, at the same firm or a different one.
An amount that the rules say must be taken out of certain retirement accounts each year after a set age. An advisor can explain whether it applies to you.
also_heard_as: the amount I have to take out

glossary.plain: A professional who helps you plan and make decisions about your money and investments.
Someone you name whom the firm may reach out to if it cannot reach you or is concerned about your account. They cannot make changes or trades for you.
also_heard_as: someone you can call about me
